title: High-order resonances and emergent coherent dynamics in interacting Stark chains
abstract: A linear potential gradient can strongly suppress quantum dynamics, while interactions can activate resonant many-body processes whose higher-order structure remains largely unexplored. Here we uncover a systematic hierarchy of high-order interaction--tilt resonances in an interacting Stark chain, where the resonance order counts the minimal number of elementary exchange steps involved. These resonances manifest as long-lived coherent oscillations with order-dependent timescales. By isolating individual resonant channels and developing a microscopic effective description, we connect these dynamical timescales to the underlying many-body exchange processes and reveal a pronounced dependence on the initial-state structure. Our results provide crucial insights into high-order many-body resonances and show how commensurate interaction-to-tilt ratios generate a hierarchy of parametrically slow coherent many-body dynamics.
summary: This work investigates high-order resonances in interacting quantum spin chains under a linear potential gradient (Stark effect). The authors systematically map out a hierarchy of resonances, showing they manifest as long-lived coherent oscillations. By deriving effective Hamiltonians, they provide a microscopic understanding of how specific interaction-to-tilt ratios stabilize these slow, coherent many-body dynamics.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically classify and microscopically describe high-order interaction-tilt resonances in interacting quantum spin chains subjected to a linear potential gradient (Stark effect).
main_result: The authors uncover a hierarchy of high-order resonances characterized by long-lived, coherent many-body oscillations whose timescales depend parametrically on the resonance order and the ratio of interaction to tilt strength.
method: The analysis employs quench dynamics simulations using TEBD and develops an effective Hamiltonian via high-frequency expansion and perturbation theory to calculate resonant coupling strengths.
model_or_system: The system is an interacting Stark spin chain, modeled by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor interactions (Ising term $\Delta$) and a linear potential gradient ($W$). The dynamics are analyzed by mapping the system to a fermionic Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Localization length ($\xi(t)$), average localization length ($ ar{\xi}$), fluctuation measure ($\sigma^2_{\xi}$), and the dominant frequency ($\omega_{	ext{dom}}$).
important_parameters: The resonance condition is governed by the fractional ratio $\Delta/W = p/q$, and the resonance order $n$ dictates the scaling of the dominant frequency ($\omega_{	ext{dom}} \sim W^{-(n-1)}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-frequency expansion and perturbation theory (Schrieffer-Wolff), which is systematic but computationally intensive for very high orders.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three dynamical regimes (smooth, coherent, suppressed) via magnetization profiles, and show the resonance signatures in localization length maps ($ ar{\xi}$ and $\sigma^2_{\xi}$) at specific $\Delta/W$ ratios.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general dynamic characterization using localization length to deriving an effective Hamiltonian via perturbation theory, culminating in the calculation of specific resonant coupling strengths for higher-order processes.
why_interesting: The connection between commensurately tuned interaction-to-tilt ratios and the emergence of parametrically slow, coherent many-body dynamics is highly relevant for understanding controllable quantum simulation platforms.

FIG. 3. Time-rescaled collapse of resonant dynamics. At fixed ∆/W = p/q, the local magnetization ⟨Sz 0(t)⟩for different W approximately collapses under the rescaling τ = t/W nmin−1. Panels (a) and (b) correspond to p/q = 5/2 and 3/2, with nmin = 5 and 3, respectively. The black dashed curve in panel (b) is obtained from the third-order effective Hamilto- nian described below and closely reproduces the full-model dynamics. The collapse confirms that nmin sets the charac- teristic dynamical timescale; residual deviations arise from subleading higher-order corrections.

FIG. 4. Dominant-frequency scaling of the resonant dynam- ics. (a) Dominant oscillation frequency ωdom/2π, extracted from the frequency spectrum of ⟨Sz 0(t)⟩, as a function of the Stark gradient W on log–log axes for resonance ratios p/q = 3/2, 2, and 5/2. The error bars indicate the lower and upper half-maximum frequencies of the dominant spec- tral peak. Power-law fits ωdom ∼W −α yield exponents con- sistent with the prediction α = nmin −1.
